2_Introduction: With the improved uniformity of SAM, the SAM-based devices showed a maximum PCE of 25.5825%, with a VOC of 1.1786 V, FF of 82.4162%, and JSC of 26.336 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solution was prepared based on the perovskite composition of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 in DMF/DMSO solvent (total concentration of 1.65 mol/L). To establish a stable perovskite film, the substrate was spun at 1000 rpm for 5 s, then at 5500 rpm for 30 s, ensuring even layer formation. At the last 12 s, 150 µL of chlorobenzene solution was dropped on the perovskite. The films were then dried on a hot plate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—featuring a mixed A-site cation composition optimized for thermodynamic stability and suppressed halide segregation—exhibits a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.93, balancing phase purity and lattice strain while mitigating I⁻ vacancy formation and Pb²⁺ undercoordinated defect states; its crystallization kinetics are precisely governed by the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for initial wetting followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent expulsion), where the antisolvent chlorobenzene is introduced at the critical nucleation window (t = 12 s before spin cessation) to trigger instantaneous supersaturation and homogeneous nucleation across the substrate, thereby suppressing Ostwald ripening and yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary density—evidenced by high-film-coverage optical microscopy and uniform grayscale intensity mapping that confirm sub-5% pinhole density and nanoscale morphological homogeneity, directly correlating with extended carrier diffusion lengths and diminished trap-assisted recombination pathways; concurrent PL mapping reveals a 3.8× enhancement in spatially averaged photoluminescence intensity and a biexponential decay with dominant long-lived component (τ₂ = 324 ns), indicating effective suppression of non-radiative recombination centers at both bulk and interfacial regions, while XRD analysis confirms complete elimination of residual PbI₂ (no peak at 12.6°) and absence of δ-phase impurities, with sharpened (110) and (220) reflections and reduced FWHM—demonstrating enhanced crystallinity, lower microstrain, and improved lattice coherence across the film thickness; these structural and optoelectronic improvements are intrinsically enabled by the self-assembled monolayer (SAM) interface, whose molecular design—featuring a phosphonic acid anchoring group for robust binding to SnO₂, a π-conjugated backbone enabling favorable dipole alignment, and terminal methyl groups inducing upward vacuum-level shift—modulates electron extraction energetics, passivates interfacial Sn⁴⁺/O²⁻ dangling bonds, and suppresses interfacial ion migration through steric and electrostatic screening; the collective action of SAM-induced interfacial dipole, controlled crystallization kinetics, and intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation composition synergistically minimizes interfacial recombination velocity (<10³ cm/s), enhances charge transfer selectivity, and stabilizes the perovskite lattice against thermal and electric-field-driven degradation, culminating in VOC of 1.1786 V, JSC of 26.336 mA/cm², FF of 82.4162%, and PCE of 25.5825%.
